text:
Artificial intelligence has created new opportunities for language education. AI-powered applications can provide translation, pronunciation feedback, grammar correction, and personalised conversation practice. These tools allow students to practise more frequently and receive support outside the classroom. However, successful language learning still requires meaningful communication and cultural understanding.

One major advantage of AI is accessibility. Students can practise a language at any time without depending on the availability of a teacher or conversation partner. Chatbots can simulate everyday situations such as ordering food, attending an interview, or asking for directions. This repeated practice may increase confidence and reduce anxiety, particularly among learners who are uncomfortable speaking in front of others.

AI can also provide targeted feedback. Language platforms may identify recurring grammar mistakes, pronunciation difficulties, or vocabulary gaps. Exercises can then be adjusted according to the learner’s performance. Such personalisation is difficult to provide consistently in large classes where teachers must divide their attention among many students.

Nevertheless, AI-generated communication may not fully reflect natural language use. Real conversations include humour, emotion, cultural references, accents, and unexpected responses. A learner who practises only with AI may develop technically correct language but struggle in complex social situations.

There is also a risk of overdependence on translation and correction tools. Students may accept improved sentences without understanding why changes were made. Teachers should therefore require learners to review corrections, explain errors, and apply the same principles independently.

AI can improve language learning by expanding access to practice and personalised feedback. However, it should complement rather than replace interaction with teachers and human speakers. Language is not only a technical system; it is also a social and cultural form of communication.
